title: Can Nuclear Fuel Be Delivered in Time to Power Advanced Nuclear Reactors?
gist: Nuclear fuel industry veteran Elmer Dyke argues that HALEU fuel supply is a top risk for Western advanced small modular reactors (ASMRs): no commercial HALEU market exists, CAT2 plants are costly, suppliers won't build without guaranteed contracts, and Western uranium conversion is short after the shift away from Russian fuel. He expects Western commercial HALEU only in the early 2030s, says HALEU will never cost as little as LEU, and concludes government stimulus (offtakes, cost-sharing, deconversion funding) is needed so reactors and fuel arrive together, while Russia and China hold a lead.

insights.claim: Conditions for nuclear expansion are the most favorable in decades, driven by energy security after Russia's invasion of Ukraine and the US-Israeli war with Iran, and by surging electricity demand from data centers and AI.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: AI-driven power demand plus security concerns underpin the nuclear investment cycle.
insights.quote: Renewed enthusiasm for nuclear power is being driven by global emphasis on energy security following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and by surging electricity demand

insights.claim: There are more than eighty SMR designs worldwide, but only China and Russia have deployed commercial advanced SMRs, and both are offering designs to global customers.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Russia and China lead in exportable advanced reactor technology, a geopolitical and commercial edge over Western vendors.
insights.quote: only China and Russia have deployed commercial ASMRs; both nations plan to expand their deployments and are offering their designs to global customers
insights.locator: There are more than eighty SMR

insights.claim: Outside Russia and China, no ASMR has final funding approval and no commercial ASMR design has Western design license approval; the US is backing TerraPower's Natrium in Wyoming and X-Energy's X-100 in Texas powering a Dow plant.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Western advanced-reactor names remain pre-commercial with unproven economics, a key risk for equity valuations.
insights.quote: Outside of Russia and China, there are no ASMRs that have final funding approval, nor have any commercial ASMR designs achieved Western design license approvals.

insights.claim: Dyke expects first-of-a-kind ASMRs to become operational in 2030-2034, with wider deployments ramping in 2035 and beyond only if early units prove constructability and cost performance.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Meaningful revenue for advanced reactor developers is a 2030s story, not near term.
insights.quote: a reasonable expectation is to see early FOAK ASMRs of various types becoming operational in 2030 to 2034, with more widespread deployments quickly ramping up for successfully operating ASMRs in 2035 and beyond
insights.locator: These expected near- to mid-term deployments

insights.claim: Light water reactor SMRs using standard LEU fuel are likely to deploy faster and at higher volumes than ASMRs because of existing licensing, supply chains and fuel cycles.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Near-term SMR winners are more likely LWR-based designs than HALEU-dependent ones.
insights.quote: Even as ASMR development continues, LWR SMRs could be deployed more quickly and at higher volumes
insights.locator: These expected near- to mid-term deployments

insights.claim: NuScale reports investing over $1.8 billion, including DOE grants, to de-risk its technology and obtain NRC approval, yet its design is still incomplete and years from first operation, illustrating extreme development costs.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Reactor developers face multi-billion, multi-year cash burn before revenue.

insights.claim: Technology firms needing power for AI and data centers are providing offtakes and investments in ASMRs, the EU in 2025 classified nuclear as a sustainable investment, and the European Investment Bank is increasing nuclear lending.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Financing channels for nuclear are broadening across tech offtakers and public lenders.
insights.quote: Technology firms (especially those needing massive power for AI and data centers) are providing some financial incentives, offtakes, and investments in the ASMR market.

insights.claim: The HALEU fuel industry faces a chicken-and-egg dilemma: reactors need fuel, but suppliers will not build costly fuel plants without a proven market.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Fuel availability is a gating constraint that can delay advanced reactor deployments regardless of reactor readiness.
insights.quote: Fuel is required to run the reactors, but suppliers hesitate to build costly fuel plants without a proven market.

insights.claim: Urenco has begun building a HALEU enrichment plant in the UK, but there are no HALEU deconversion plants for uranium oxide or metal and no HALEU fuel fabrication plants under construction.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Deconversion is a missing link in the Western HALEU chain, creating a bottleneck opportunity for whoever builds it.
insights.quote: to date there are no HALEU deconversion plants for either uranium oxide or uranium metal that will be required for final fuel assembly, nor are HALEU fuel fabrication plants under construction

insights.claim: If fuel supply and reactor deployments do not line up, investors, industrial end users and utilities will hesitate before launching additional ASMRs.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: A fuel-timing mismatch could stall the second wave of advanced reactor orders.
insights.quote: If the fuel supply and reactor deployments do not line up, investors, new end users such as industrial firms, and utilities will hesitate before launching additional ASMR reactors.

insights.claim: Western HALEU suppliers will only build plants with bankable long-term take-or-pay contracts or milestone pre-payments, while pre-revenue ASMR designers cannot afford to fund fuel production themselves.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Government-backed offtake is the likely unlock for HALEU capacity investment.
insights.quote: The suppliers are more than willing to build new or to expand existing production plants if they receive bankable, guaranteed long-term contracts, but to date this has not happened on a large scale for HALEU fuel.

insights.claim: Commercial HALEU fuel cycle suppliers will not build plants until there is an understandable market, sufficient long-term demand, and guaranteed contracts with financially sound entities.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: A clear checklist for when to expect private HALEU capex to accelerate.
insights.quote: 1) there is an understandable market; 2) there exists sufficient long-term demand from this market; 3) there are guaranteed contracts with financially sound entities

insights.claim: HALEU (10-19.75 percent U-235) must be produced in Category 2 facilities with much stricter safety, safeguards and security than the Category 3 plants used for LEU, raising construction and operating costs and lowering throughput.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Structurally higher fuel costs weigh on ASMR operating economics.
insights.quote: HALEU fuel therefore must be produced in much costlier Category 2 (CAT2) facilities that are highly engineered for more stringent safety, safeguards, and security conditions than CAT3 facilities
insights.locator: Traditional LWRs typically use nuclear fuel

insights.claim: Dyke contrarily asserts that HALEU fuel will never cost as little as LEU, because HALEU volumes will always be far smaller and CAT2 facilities always more expensive, despite many ASMR designers expecting parity.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: ASMR business plans assuming LEU-like fuel costs are likely too optimistic.
insights.quote: Many ASMR designers initially expected—and some still expect—HALEU fuel costs to be comparable to LEU fuel costs. This will never occur for two reasons

insights.claim: About 4.5 kilograms of LEU are needed to make 1 kilogram of 19.75 percent HALEU, and roughly 85 percent of the separative work goes into the first 4.95 percent enrichment, so HALEU costs cannot fall much unless LEU costs fall first.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: HALEU economics are levered to the LEU enrichment market, linking ASMR fuel costs to existing enrichment pricing.
insights.quote: Approximately 4.5 kilograms of LEU are needed to make 1 kilogram of HALEU at 19.75 percent U-235; thus, for HALEU fuel costs to drop significantly, LEU costs must drop first.

insights.claim: The LEU enrichment market is about 50,000 metric tons of separative work units, while firm HALEU demand is nonexistent today and may not exceed 100 metric tons until the early to mid-2030s.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: HALEU will remain a niche market for years, limiting scale economies for producers.
insights.quote: HALEU demand may not exceed 100 MT HALEU until the early to mid-2030s, assuming current ASMR projects actually reach fruition

insights.claim: The Natrium reactor needs roughly 15 metric tons of HALEU for its first core, whereas microreactors may need only hundreds of kilograms, so microreactors will not drive commercial HALEU supply development.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Larger ASMRs, not microreactors, will determine HALEU demand and supplier investment.
insights.quote: the Natrium reactor will need roughly 15 metric tons of HALEU for the first core, while micro-ASMRs may need only hundreds of kilograms of HALEU

insights.claim: Russia supplied around 25 percent of US and European nuclear fuel for decades; with the West shifting away since February 2022, Western natural UF6 production is insufficient to meet Western commercial demand, and ASMR demand will widen the deficit.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Structural Western conversion and uranium deficits support pricing power for Western fuel cycle suppliers.
insights.quote: there is not sufficient Western natural UF₆ production to meet Western commercial demand, meaning that any additional fuel demand arising from ASMR deployments will add to existing and projected future Western UF₆ supply deficits

insights.claim: The only Western uranium conversion producers are Cameco in Canada, ConverDyn in the US and Orano in France, and the West is woefully short of conversion capacity with little quick movement to expand.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Concentrated Western conversion capacity is a chokepoint benefitting incumbents like Cameco and Orano.
insights.quote: The only Western conversion producers are Cameco in Canada, ConverDyn in the United States, and Orano in France. The West is woefully short of sufficient conversion to meet Western demand
insights.locator: Many forget the necessity of the LEU

insights.claim: A 2023 coup in Niger led to the transfer of the country's uranium mine operations from France's Orano to Russia, highlighting geopolitical competition over uranium supply.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Uranium supply from non-aligned producers carries political risk that can redirect volumes to Russia/China.
insights.quote: The tension over uranium supply was highlighted by a 2023 coup in Niger, which resulted in the transfer of operation of the country’s uranium mines from the French firm Orano to Russia.
insights.locator: Many forget the necessity of the LEU

insights.claim: When fuel supply is tight, existing utility customers will get preferred status from fuel cycle suppliers, so new ASMR developers will struggle to compete for uranium, conversion and enrichment.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Newcomer reactor developers face supply-access risk beyond price.
insights.quote: For the most part, if fuel supply is tight, existing utility companies will have preferred status. Suppliers will not turn their collective backs on their long-term customers.
insights.locator: Further, governmental support will be needed

insights.claim: In 2025 the UK awarded Urenco a £196 million HALEU enrichment contract for a cascade at Capenhurst, expected online in 2031 or 2032, but has not yet funded HALEU deconversion.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: UK HALEU supply is a 2030s event, with deconversion still a gap.
insights.quote: In 2025, the UK government awarded a HALEU enrichment contract valued at £196 million to Urenco to support the deployment of a HALEU enrichment cascade at Capenhurst.

insights.claim: In January 2026 the US DOE awarded two HALEU enrichment contracts of $900 million each to Centrus and General Matter, and intends to issue deconversion awards in 2026, with six US firms competing.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Federal contracts de-risk HALEU enrichment buildout for Centrus and General Matter.
insights.quote: in January 2026 the DOE awarded two HALEU enrichment contracts valued at $900 million each to Centrus and General Matter

insights.claim: Initial commercial HALEU production could begin in 2029 and ramp through the early 2030s, but Dyke judges reliable Western commercial production unlikely before 2030 and deconversion plants likely need four years from design to operation.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Fuel timing leaves little slack for first ASMR fuel loads around 2030.
insights.quote: by current estimates commercial production is unlikely to be reliable until 2030 or beyond
insights.locator: Western suppliers will continue to rely

insights.claim: Russia and China will be able to produce commercial HALEU faster than Western suppliers and will likely package ASMR designs with fuel supply, though geopolitics may limit their reach to select markets such as Eurasia and Africa.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Russia and China could lock in emerging-market nuclear customers via reactor-plus-fuel bundles.
insights.quote: Both Russia and China will be able to produce commercial quantities of HALEU in the near term faster than Western suppliers, but geopolitical issues could constrain their expansion in global markets
insights.locator: Although Russia and China have only

insights.claim: China has so far depended on Russia for commercial quantities of HALEU and would need a few years to deliver commercial quantities reliably itself.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Russia is the dominant current HALEU supplier globally, reinforcing its leverage in nuclear fuel.
insights.quote: To date, China has depended on Russia to supply commercial quantities of HALEU fuel.

insights.claim: Dyke argues governments must fill the near-term gap with offtake agreements, cost-sharing, grants, low-cost loans and milestone payments for HALEU and LEU capacity, since pre-revenue startups cannot fund fuel cycle buildout.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Policy support is the key catalyst to watch for fuel cycle and advanced reactor equities.
insights.quote: Few commercial firms can take this risk alone, and by their nature, pre-revenue startup firms cannot fund fuel cycle and supply chain buildout. Governments can and should fill the near-term gap.
insights.locator: Further, governmental support will be needed

insights.claim: Dyke notes the US government's initial vision of guaranteeing HALEU demand via long-term offtake morphed into supporting HALEU capacity deployment instead, and argues incentives must be large and long-lasting since fuel plants operate for decades.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Capacity grants without demand guarantees may not fully unlock private fuel investment.
insights.quote: While this appears to have been the initial vision of the U.S. government, that approach morphed into supporting the deployment of HALEU capacity instead.
insights.locator: HALEU fuel supply remains a critical

insights.claim: Russia and China benefit from consistent policy and state ownership of the nuclear sector, while Western deployment requires government support that survives administrative transitions.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Western nuclear programs carry political-cycle risk that state-led rivals avoid.

insights.claim: China's HTGR, connected to the grid in 2023, has averaged only a 26.9 percent availability factor versus US reactor capacity factors above 90 percent since 2000, largely due to fuel problems, echoing failures at Fort St. Vrain and Peach Bottom.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Fuel quality risk can make novel reactors uneconomic, a cautionary benchmark for ASMR investors.
insights.quote: the reactor subsequently has averaged only a 26.9 percent availability factor

insights.claim: ASMRs will almost certainly be less economical than large LWRs but can offset this through faster deployment and modularity, provided regulators harmonize licensing and designers avoid bespoke designs.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: ASMR value proposition rests on speed and standardization, not unit cost.
insights.quote: ASMRs will almost certainly be less economical than large LWRs, but can offset this with faster deployment timelines and modularity.
insights.locator: For ASMRs to be deployed competitively

insights.claim: Dyke says the failure to standardize Western LWR designs caused major delays and cost overruns, and ASMR designers must avoid this bespoke-design trap.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Vendors pursuing standardized global designs should have cost advantages.
insights.quote: The failure to develop standardized designs among Western LWRs has been a mistake, leading to major delays and cost overruns.

insights.claim: If the ASMR market materializes, potentially dozens of new nations could host and operate CAT2 HALEU facilities by 2040, some without prior commercial reactor experience, requiring safeguards and nonproliferation regimes to adapt in advance.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Proliferation concerns could trigger regulatory tightening that slows ASMR exports.
insights.quote: If the market materializes, potentially dozens of new nations could emerge by 2040 to host, operate, and manage CAT2 facilities.

insights.claim: Used fuel management for ASMRs is unresolved; some designs may produce more used fuel volume with lower radiotoxicity, while others could produce more plutonium in used fuel.
insights.speaker: Elmer W. Dyke
insights.so_what: Waste and plutonium issues are an underappreciated licensing and public-acceptance risk.
insights.quote: ASMRs in some cases are expected to produce more used fuel volume but less radiotoxicity, though in some cases they could produce more plutonium in used fuel
